stories.title: OpenAI raises $11 billion in funding round valuing it at $1.25 trillion
stories.summary: OpenAI has secured $11 billion so far in a new funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion, according to Bloomberg as reported by TechCrunch. The $11 billion is part of a larger round that has not yet closed and may total about $20 billion, below the $30 billion target mentioned in September. OpenAI has not responded to comment requests.
stories.why: The funding could enable OpenAI to expand development and deployment of its advanced AI models.
stories.previousSummary: OpenAI has reportedly secured $11 billion in a funding round that values the company at $1.25 trillion. The round is still open and Bloomberg expects it could close in the coming weeks with total commitments around $20 billion, below the earlier September target of $30 billion. TechCrunch has asked OpenAI for comment and is awaiting a response.

stories.title: Google buys unfinished Wyoming data center project from Crusoe
stories.summary: Crusoe, a Denver‑based data‑center developer valued at $30.9 billion, confirmed it sold its unfinished data‑center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. Google, which Crusoe had previously tried to win as a customer, will take over development and has announced a $17 billion investment to build the campus. The project was originally announced with Tallgrass to eventually reach 10 GW of capacity.
stories.why: The transaction illustrates the challenges independent developers face delivering large‑scale data‑center projects and shows Google’s commitment to expanding its infrastructure capacity.
stories.previousTitle: Google buys unfinished Wyoming data center project from Crusoe
stories.previousSummary: Denver‑based data center developer Crusoe confirmed it has sold an unfinished data center project in southeastern Wyoming to Google. The project, announced last year with Blackstone‑backed Tallgrass and planned to eventually reach 10 GW of power capacity, faced cost and timeline concerns under Crusoe’s management. Google did not disclose the purchase price but announced a $17 billion investment to develop the campus.
